turns.content: Hey, can I ask you something kind of trivial? Last night my roommate told me she's staying at her new guy's place on Friday instead of our usual movie night, and I think I reacted a little weird. I just said "cool, have fun" and went to bed early. Does that come off as passive-aggressive, or am I overthinking it?

“Cool, have fun” followed by going to bed early is not inherently passive-aggressive. It could be read that way if your tone was clipped, if you normally stay up later, or if there was existing tension, but the behavior alone does not establish intent.

If you think it landed poorly, a brief clarification is proportionate:

> “I realized I might’ve seemed abrupt last night. I was a little disappointed about missing movie night, but I wasn’t trying to make you feel bad. I hope you have fun Friday.”

That states your reaction without accusing her or turning it into a larger conflict.

Hmm, so you think it could go either way depending on tone? That's actually kind of what I was worried about... I don't think I sounded angry, but I did kind of cut the conversation short. Should I just let it go or say something this morning?

Because you cut the conversation short, she could have interpreted it as disappointment, tiredness, or irritation; there is no evidence that she did.

If things seem normal this morning, let it go and behave normally. If she seems distant, mentions it, or you want to prevent ambiguity, say one sentence:

> “I realized I ended the conversation pretty abruptly last night—I was disappointed about missing movie night, but I’m not upset with you.”

Avoid a long apology unless she indicates that it affected her.
Well, she just sent a normal good morning text asking if I want coffee. So probably no damage done, right? Or am I reading too much into her being normal?

Her normal text and coffee offer provide no indication that she took offense. They cannot prove what she thought, but there is no current reason to treat this as a problem.

Reply normally and accept or decline the coffee. No clarification is needed unless she raises last night or her behavior changes.
Alright, so you think I'm fine to just take the coffee and act normal? No need to even mention last night unless she does?
Yes. Based on her normal message and coffee offer, reply normally and do not raise last night unless she does. There is no evidence of a conflict that needs resolving.
Hmm, that makes sense. But what if she brings up last night first? Should I just brush it off or actually admit I was a little disappointed?

If she brings it up, acknowledge the disappointment rather than brushing it off. Keep it brief and separate your feeling from blame:

> “Yeah, I was a little disappointed that movie night changed, so I probably ended the conversation abruptly. I’m not angry with you, though, and I hope you have a good time.”

If she says your response felt pointed, add:

> “I can see how it came across that way. I should have said what I meant directly.”

This addresses the observable behavior without turning her plans into wrongdoing.
